other_quotes.quote: 24.01.120 - Exemption for pending applications. A. The provisions of the 2025 California Building, Residential, Plumbing, Mechanical, Electrical ... Codes ... as adopted and amended herein, shall not apply to any building or structure for which application for a building permit was made prior to January 1, 2026.

building.note: The city's building code amendments (Chapter 24.03, Parts 2 to 8) cover covered malls, high-rises, atriums, stages, fire-resistance-rated construction, sprinklers, structural design, special inspections and gypsum board. None touches toilet rooms, interior finishes or plumbing fixture counts. San Jose does not adopt the state code's administrative sections on permits (1.8.4 and others): its own permit rules are in Municipal Code Chapter 24.02.

permit.exempt_list_quote: 24.02.120 Building Permit Exemptions. A. A building permit shall not be required for the following: 1. One-story detached accessory buildings used as tool and storage sheds, playhouses and similar uses, provided the floor area does not exceed 120 square feet (11.15 m2). It is permissible that these structures still be regulated by Part 7 California Wildland-Urban Interface Code despite exemption from permit. 2. Fences, other than swimming pool barriers, not over seven feet (2,134 mm) high. 3. Oil derricks. 4. Nonfixed and movable fixtures cases, racks, counters and partitions not over five feet nine inches (1,753 mm) high. 5. Retaining walls which are not over four feet (1,219 mm) in height measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall, unless supporting a surcharge or impounding Class I, II or III-A liquids. 6. Water tanks supported directly upon grade if the capacity does not exceed five thousand gallons (18,925 liters) and the ratio of height to diameter or width does not exceed two to one. 7. Sidewalks and driveways not more than thirty inches (762 mm) above adjacent grade and not over any basement or story below and are not part of an accessible route. 8. Decks, in Group R-3 occupancy, not exceeding 200 square feet in area, that are not more than 30 inches above grade at any point, are not attached to a dwelling and do not serve the required exit door. 9. Painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops and similar finish work. 10. Temporary motion picture, television and theater stage sets and scenery. 11. Window awnings, in Group R-3 and U occupancies, supported by an exterior wall that do not project more than fifty-four inches from the exterior wall and do not require additional support. 12. Prefabricated swimming pools accessory to a Group R-3 occupancy that are less than 24 inches deep, are not greater than 5,000 gallons and are installed entirely above ground. 13. Replacement, repair or overlay of less than twenty-five percent of an existing roof within any twelve-month period. 14. Swings and other playground equipment accessory to detached one- and two-family dwellings. 15. Taping joints and sheetrock installations for unrated walls and ceilings. B. Unless otherwise exempted by this title, separate plumbing, electrical and mechanical permits will be required for the above exempted items.

(Ord. 28166.)

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to San Jose job sites. Price your restroom in five questions and see the California and city rules that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for San Jose tech offices, schools, restaurants and warehouses, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** San Jose uses California's rules, which set the number of toilets and urinals by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** San Jose requires a building permit to alter or repair a building unless the work is on its exempt list. The list covers "painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops and similar finish work" and movable "partitions not over five feet nine inches" high. It doesn't name toilet partitions, so ask the city's Permit Center (408-535-3555) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: the City of San Jose Building Division
page.stalls_intro: San Jose counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women, and California's rules require urinals in the men's room. Every toilet needs a stall, and urinals need screens between them. The women's room must have at least as many toilets as the men's room has toilets and urinals together.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for new buildings, additions and changes of use that bring in more people. An office or shop with 50 people or fewer may have a single one-person restroom. At least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, California's plumbing rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, and a restaurant dining room or a classroom at one per 30 square feet. Your architect or the City of San Jose Building Division sets the final number.
page.install_rule: San Jose's building code sets no city contractor license. California requires its contractor license, usually the C-61/D-34 class, for partition installs of $1,000 or more, and at any price when the job needs workers or a permit. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: In San Jose the contractor needs a California contractor license for jobs of $1,000 or more.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** California requires the state-set wage on public jobs over $1,000, including city and school district work. For a carpenter in Santa Clara County that is $74.46 an hour plus $34.95 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 10% in San Jose: 7.25% statewide, 2.5% in Santa Clara County district taxes and 0.25% city.
page.buyers_extra: - **Tech campuses and research buildings:** phenolic or stainless steel in a finish that matches the rest of the fit-out.
